newsitem.title: UK: Jersey says collective funds top 33 billion stg.
newsitem.headline: Jersey says collective funds top 33 billion stg.

text.p: Funds under management in Jersey's investment industry rose by 2.6 billion sterling to 33.3 billion sterling in the first quarter of 1997, Jersey's financial services department said on Tuesday.
Gross sales by the island's fund management industry were 4.8 billion sterling, with net sales of 1.7 billion.

"This large inflow, coupled with positive returns from many of the world's investment markets and a strong dollar, has helped raise funds under management by 2.6 billion sterling," said Jonathan Overland, Jersey Fund Managers Association publicity officer.
Jersey said the number of funds on the island fell to 332 from 346 in the period, although the number of sub-funds or investment pools rose to a record 1,017 from 992.
Equity funds attracted the largest net inflow of 737 million sterling, with the majority of that - 427 million - invested in continental Europe.
Money market funds, real property funds and international bond funds were also popular.
In terms of funds under management, money market funds were up 0.9 billion, European equities up 0.7 billion, and real property up 0.7 billion.

Financial services deputy director John Pallot said an increasing number of countries were recognising Jersey funds for marketing into their jurisdiction, including Japan, the Netherlands, Austria, Hong Kong and most recently Australia.
